title.zh: 卷八十七 列傳第十七: 蕭孝穆 蕭蒲奴 耶律蒲古 夏行美
title.raw: 卷八十七 列傳第十七: 蕭孝穆 蕭蒲奴 耶律蒲古 夏行美 Volume 87 Biographies 17:

sentences.zh: 蕭孝穆

translations.literal: Xiao Xiaomu
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xiaomu

sentences.zh: （撒八孝先孝友）〉

translations.literal: (Saba, Xiaoxian, and Xiaoyou have separate biographies)〉
translations.idiomatic: (See the biographies of Saba, Xiaoxian, and Xiaoyou)〉

sentences.zh: 蕭蒲奴耶律蒲古夏行美

translations.literal: Xiao Punu, Yelü Pugu, Xia Xingmei
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Punu, Yelü Pugu, and Xia Xingmei

sentences.zh: 蕭孝穆，小字胡獨堇，淳欽皇后弟阿古只五世孫。

translations.literal: Xiao Xiaomu, childhood name Hudujin, was a fifth-generation descendant of Aguzhi, younger brother of Empress Chunqin.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xiaomu, whose childhood name was Hudujin, was a fifth-generation descendant of Aguzhi, the younger brother of Empress Chunqin.

sentences.zh: 父陶瑰，為國舅詳穩。

translations.literal: His father Taogui served as Detailed Commandant of the Imperial Maternal Clan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Taogui held the post of Detailed Commandant of the Imperial Maternal Clan.

sentences.zh: 孝穆廉謹有禮法。

translations.literal: Xiaomu was incorruptible, cautious, and observant of ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaomu was upright and discreet, and he upheld ritual and law.

sentences.zh: 統和二十八年，累遷西北路招討都監。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year of the Tonghe era, he was repeatedly promoted to Pacification Commissioner-in-Chief of the Northwest Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year of Tonghe, he rose through successive appointments to Pacification Commissioner-in-Chief of the Northwest Circuit.

sentences.zh: 開泰元年，遙授建雄軍節度使，加檢校太保。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaitai, he was appointed in absentia Military Commissioner of the Jianxiong Army, with the additional title of Grand Guardian of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaitai, he received a remote appointment as Military Commissioner of the Jianxiong Army and was given the additional rank of Grand Guardian of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 是年術烈等變，孝穆擊走之。

translations.literal: That year, when Shulie and others rebelled, Xiaomu routed them.
translations.idiomatic: That same year, when Shulie and others rose in revolt, Xiaomu drove them off.

sentences.zh: 冬，進軍可敦城。

translations.literal: In winter, the army advanced to Kedun City.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he marched on Kedun City.

sentences.zh: 阻卜結五群牧長查剌、阿睹等，謀中外相應，孝穆悉誅之，乃嚴備禦以待，餘黨遂潰。

translations.literal: The Zubu chieftains Zhala, Adu, and others of five herds plotted to coordinate inside and outside; Xiaomu executed them all, then made strict preparations to await them, and the remaining conspirators dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhala, Adu, and other chieftains of five Zubu herds plotted to act in concert within and beyond the borders. Xiaomu put them all to death, tightened defenses, and waited; the rest of the plotters then broke apart.

sentences.zh: 以功遷九水諸部安撫使。

translations.literal: For his merit he was transferred to Commissioner for Pacification of the Nine-Water Tribes.
translations.idiomatic: For this achievement he was made Commissioner for Pacification of the Nine-Water Tribes.

sentences.zh: 尋拜北府宰相，賜忠穆熙霸功臣，檢校太師，同政事門下平章事。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Chancellor of the Northern Commission, granted the title of Meritous Minister Zhongmu Xiba, Grand Preceptor of Ceremonies, and Associate in the Department of Affairs with the title Equalizer-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon named Chancellor of the Northern Commission, granted the merit title Zhongmu Xiba, made Grand Preceptor of Ceremonies, and appointed Associate in the Department of Affairs with the title Equalizer-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 八年，還京師。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 太平二年，知樞密院事，充漢人行宮都部署。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping, he served as Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and as Chief Deployment Commissioner of the Chinese Palatial Camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiping he took charge of the Bureau of Military Affairs and served as Chief Deployment Commissioner of the Chinese Palatial Camp.

sentences.zh: 三年，封燕王、南京留守、兵馬都總管。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yan, made Military Governor of Nanjing, and appointed Commander-in-Chief of all forces.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yan, appointed Military Governor of Nanjing, and made Commander-in-Chief of all forces.

sentences.zh: 九年，大延琳以東京叛，孝穆為都統討之，戰於蒲水。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, when Da Yanlin rebelled at Dongjing, Xiaomu was made Commander-in-Chief to suppress him and fought at the Pu River.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, when Da Yanlin rebelled at Dongjing, the Eastern Capital, Xiaomu was appointed overall commander to suppress him and gave battle at the Pu River.

sentences.zh: 中軍稍卻，副部署蕭匹敵、都監蕭蒲奴以兩翼夾擊，賊潰，追敗之於手山北。

translations.literal: The center army fell back slightly; Deputy Deployment Commissioner Xiao Pidi and Commissioner Xiao Punu struck from both wings, the rebels were routed, and they were pursued and defeated north of Mount Shou.
translations.idiomatic: When the center gave ground, Deputy Deployment Commissioner Xiao Pidi and Commissioner Xiao Punu attacked from both flanks. The rebels broke, and the pursuers crushed them north of Mount Shou.

sentences.zh: 延琳走入城，深溝自衛。

translations.literal: Yanlin fled into the city and dug deep moats to defend himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yanlin retreated into the city and dug deep trenches to hold his ground.

sentences.zh: 孝穆圍之，築重城，起樓櫓，使內外不相通，城中撤屋以爨。

translations.literal: Xiaomu besieged it, built layered walls, raised siege towers, cut off communication inside and outside, and within the city they tore down houses for fuel.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaomu laid siege, threw up outer walls and siege towers, and severed all contact between the city and the outside world. Inside, the defenders pulled down houses for firewood.

sentences.zh: 其將楊詳世等擒延琳以降，遼東悉平。

translations.literal: His generals Yang Xiangshi and others seized Yanlin and surrendered; Liaodong was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: His officers Yang Xiangshi and others captured Yanlin and submitted; all of Liaodong was pacified.

sentences.zh: 改東京留守，賜佐國功臣。

translations.literal: He was made Military Governor of Dongjing and granted the merit title Assisting the State.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Military Governor of Dongjing and granted the merit title Assisting the State.

sentences.zh: 為政務寬簡，撫納流徙，其民安之。

translations.literal: In governing he was broad and simple, comforted and received displaced people, and the people were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: His administration was lenient and straightforward; he welcomed and settled displaced people, and the populace lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 孝穆雖椒房親，位高益畏。

translations.literal: Although Xiaomu was a maternal-clan kinsman, the higher his position, the more fearful he became.
translations.idiomatic: Though Xiaomu was of the empress's clan, the higher he rose, the more cautious he became.

sentences.zh: 太后有賜，輒辭不受。

translations.literal: Whenever the Empress Dowager bestowed gifts, he invariably declined them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Empress Dowager offered him gifts, he refused them.

sentences.zh: 妻子無驕色。

translations.literal: His wife and children showed no arrogance.
translations.idiomatic: Neither his wife nor his children showed the least arrogance.

sentences.zh: 與人交，始終如一。

translations.literal: In dealings with others he was consistent from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: In his dealings with others he was steadfast from first to last.

sentences.zh: 所薦拔皆忠直士。

translations.literal: Those he recommended and promoted were all loyal and upright men.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone he recommended for office was loyal and upright.

sentences.zh: 嘗語人曰：「樞密選賢而用，何事不濟？

translations.literal: He once said to others: "If the Bureau of Military Affairs selects the worthy and employs them, what affair will not succeed?
translations.idiomatic: He once told others, "If the Bureau of Military Affairs chooses able men and puts them to use, what task will not succeed?

sentences.zh: 若自親煩碎，則大事疑滯矣。

translations.literal: If one personally attends to trivial matters, then great affairs will be delayed and obstructed."
translations.idiomatic: But if you take on petty details yourself, great affairs will stall."

sentences.zh: 」自蕭合卓以吏才進，其後轉效，不知大體。

translations.literal: Since Xiao Hezhuo advanced through clerical talent, those after him followed suit and did not understand the larger principles.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiao Hezhuo rose through clerical skill alone, others imitated him and lost sight of the larger principles of governance.

sentences.zh: 嘆曰：「不能移風易俗，偷安爵位，臣子之道若是乎？

translations.literal: He sighed and said: "Unable to transform customs and reform habits, content merely to cling to rank and salary—is this what the way of a subject should be?
translations.idiomatic: He sighed and said, "Unable to transform customs and reform habits, content merely to cling to rank and salary—is this what the way of a subject should be?

sentences.zh: 」時稱為「國寶臣」，目所著文曰《寶老集》。

translations.literal: " At the time he was called a "national treasure minister," and his collected writings were titled 《Collected Works of the Treasure Elder》.
translations.idiomatic: " His contemporaries called him a "national treasure minister," and they referred to his collected writings as 《Collected Works of the Treasure Elder》.

sentences.zh: 二子阿剌、撒八，弟孝先、孝忠、孝友，各有傳。

translations.literal: His two sons Ala and Saba, and his younger brothers Xiaoxian, Xiaozhong, and Xiaoyou, each have separate biographies.
translations.idiomatic: His two sons Ala and Saba, and his younger brothers Xiaoxian, Xiaozhong, and Xiaoyou, each have their own biographies.

sentences.zh: 孝先，字延寧，小字海裏。

translations.literal: Xiaoxian, style name Yanning, childhood name Haili.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoxian, whose style name was Yanning and whose childhood name was Haili.

sentences.zh: 統和十八年，補祗候郎君。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Tonghe, he was appointed Attendant Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Tonghe he was appointed Attendant Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 尚南陽公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: He married Princess Nanyang and was appointed Commandant of Escort.
translations.idiomatic: He married Princess Nanyang and was made Commandant of Escort.

sentences.zh: 開泰五年，為國舅詳穩。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaitai, he became Detailed Commandant of the Imperial Maternal Clan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Kaitai he became Detailed Commandant of the Imperial Maternal Clan.

sentences.zh: 將兵城東鄙。

translations.literal: He led troops to fortify the eastern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He led troops to fortify the eastern frontier.

sentences.zh: 還，為南京統軍使。

translations.literal: On his return, he was made Commander of Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed Commander of Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 太平三年，為漢人行宮都部署，尋加太子太傅。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiping, he became Chief Deployment Commissioner of the Chinese Palatial Camp and soon received the additional title of Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taiping he became Chief Deployment Commissioner of the Chinese Palatial Camp and was soon made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 五年，遷上京留守。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was transferred to Military Governor of Shangjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was transferred to Military Governor of Shangjing.

sentences.zh: 以母老求侍，復為國舅詳穩。

translations.literal: Because his mother was old, he requested to attend her and again became Detailed Commandant of the Imperial Maternal Clan.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother grew old he asked to attend her at home and again took up the post of Detailed Commandant of the Imperial Maternal Clan.

sentences.zh: 改東京留守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Military Governor of Dongjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Military Governor of Dongjing.

sentences.zh: 會大延琳反，被圍數月，穴地而出。

translations.literal: When Da Yanlin rebelled, he was besieged for several months and escaped by tunneling underground.
translations.idiomatic: When Da Yanlin rebelled, he was besieged for months before digging his way out underground.

sentences.zh: 延琳平，留守上京。

translations.literal: After Yanlin was pacified, he remained as Military Governor of Shangjing.
translations.idiomatic: After Yanlin was suppressed, he stayed on as Military Governor of Shangjing.

sentences.zh: 十一年，帝不豫，欽哀召孝先總禁衛事。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, when the Emperor was unwell, Qin'ai summoned Xiaoxian to take overall charge of the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, when the emperor fell ill, Empress Qin'ai summoned Xiaoxian to take overall charge of the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 興宗諒陰，欽哀弒仁德皇后，孝先與蕭浞卜、蕭匹敵等謀居多。

translations.literal: During Emperor Xingzong's mourning period, Qin'ai murdered Empress Rende; Xiaoxian, Xiao Fubu, Xiao Pidi, and others were chief among the conspirators.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Xingzong was in mourning, Qin'ai murdered Empress Rende; Xiaoxian, together with Xiao Fubu, Xiao Pidi, and others, played the leading part in the plot.

sentences.zh: 及欽哀攝政，遙授天平軍節度使，加守司徒，兼政事令。

translations.literal: When Qin'ai assumed regency, he was appointed in absentia Military Commissioner of the Tianping Army, made Acting Minister of Education, and concurrently Chief Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin'ai took the regency, he received a remote appointment as Military Commissioner of the Tianping Army, was made Acting Minister of Education, and served concurrently as Chief Councilor.

sentences.zh: 重熙初，封楚王，為北院樞密使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongxi, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Chu and made Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Chongxi era he was enfeoffed as Prince of Chu and appointed Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 孝先以椒房親，為太后所重。

translations.literal: Because Xiaoxian was a maternal-clan kinsman, the Empress Dowager held him in high regard.
translations.idiomatic: As a kinsman of the empress's clan, Xiaoxian enjoyed the Empress Dowager's special favor.

sentences.zh: 在樞府，好惡自恣，權傾人主，朝多側目。

translations.literal: In the Bureau of Military Affairs he indulged his likes and dislikes at will; his power overshadowed the sovereign, and many at court looked askance at him.
translations.idiomatic: At the Bureau of Military Affairs he indulged his own likes and dislikes; his power overshadowed the throne, and many at court watched him with unease.

sentences.zh: 三年，太后與孝先謀廢立事，帝知之，勒衛兵出宮，召孝先至，諭以廢太后意。

translations.literal: In the third year, the Empress Dowager and Xiaoxian plotted deposition and enthronement; the Emperor learned of it, ordered the palace guards out of the palace, summoned Xiaoxian, and informed him of his intent to depose the Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the Empress Dowager and Xiaoxian plotted to depose the emperor and enthrone another. When the emperor learned of it, he ordered the palace guards out of the palace, summoned Xiaoxian, and told him of his plan to depose the Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 孝先震懾不能對。

translations.literal: Xiaoxian was shaken with fear and could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoxian was struck dumb with fear and could not answer.

sentences.zh: 遷太后於慶州。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager was moved to Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager was sent away to Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 孝先恒郁郁不樂。

translations.literal: Xiaoxian was constantly depressed and unhappy.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoxian remained perpetually downcast.

sentences.zh: 四年，徙王晉。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, his princedom was changed to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year his title was changed from Prince of Chu to Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 後為南京留守，卒，謚忠肅。

translations.literal: Later he became Military Governor of Nanjing, died, and was given the posthumous title Loyal and Solemn.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Military Governor of Nanjing, died in office, and was posthumously titled Loyal and Solemn.

sentences.zh: 孝友，字撻不衍，小字陳留。

translations.literal: Xiaoyou, style name Tabuyan, childhood name Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyou, whose style name was Tabuyan and whose childhood name was Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 開泰初，以戚屬為小將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaitai, through imperial kinship he became a Junior General.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaitai he entered service as a Junior General through his imperial connections.

sentences.zh: 太平元年，以大冊，加左武衛大將軍、檢校太保，賜名孝友。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiping, at the great enthronement ceremony, he was made General of the Left Martial Guard, Grand Guardian of Ceremonies, and granted the name Xiaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taiping, at the grand enthronement ceremony, he was made General of the Left Martial Guard and Grand Guardian of Ceremonies and was granted the name Xiaoyou.

sentences.zh: 重熙元年，累遷西北路招討使，封蘭陵郡王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongxi, he was repeatedly promoted to Pacification Commissioner of the Northwest Circuit and enfeoffed as Prince of Lanling Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongxi he rose through successive appointments to Pacification Commissioner of the Northwest Circuit and was enfeoffed as Prince of Lanling Commandery.

sentences.zh: 八年，進王陳。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he was advanced to Prince of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was advanced to Prince of Chen.

sentences.zh: 先是，蕭惠為招討使，專以威制西羌，諸夷多叛。

translations.literal: Previously, when Xiao Hui was Pacification Commissioner, he relied solely on intimidation to control the Western Qiang, and many tribes rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Xiao Hui had been Pacification Commissioner, he had relied solely on intimidation to control the Western Qiang, and many tribes rebelled.

sentences.zh: 孝友下車，厚加綏撫，每入貢，輒增其賜物，羌人以安。

translations.literal: When Xiaoyou took office, he treated them generously with soothing measures; whenever they came to offer tribute, he always increased their gifts, and the Qiang people were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaoyou took office, he treated them with generous reassurance; whenever they came to offer tribute, he increased their gifts, and the Qiang peoples lived at peace.

sentences.zh: 久之，浸成姑息，諸夷桀驁之風遂熾，議者譏其過中。

translations.literal: Over time this gradually became excessive indulgence; the fierce and unruly ways of the tribes grew strong, and critics mocked him for going too far.
translations.idiomatic: In time his policy slid into mere indulgence; the fierce and unruly temper of the tribes grew stronger, and critics said he had gone too far.

sentences.zh: 十年，加政事令，賜效節宣庸定遠功臣，更王吳。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he was made Chief Councilor, granted the merit title Devoted in Service, Proclaiming Merit, and Settling the Distance, and his princedom was changed to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was made Chief Councilor, granted the merit title Devoted in Service, Proclaiming Merit, and Settling the Distance, and his title was changed to Prince of Wu.

sentences.zh: 後以葬兄孝穆、孝忠，還京師，拜南院樞密使，加賜翊聖協穆保義功臣，進王趙，拜中書令。

translations.literal: Later, to bury his elder brothers Xiaomu and Xiaozhong, he returned to the capital, was appointed Commissioner of the Southern Bureau of Military Affairs, granted the additional merit title Assisting the Sage, Harmonizing with Mu, and Preserving Righteousness, advanced to Prince of Zhao, and appointed Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after returning to the capital to bury his elder brothers Xiaomu and Xiaozhong, he was appointed Commissioner of the Southern Bureau of Military Affairs, granted the additional merit title Assisting the Sage, Harmonizing with Mu, and Preserving Righteousness, advanced to Prince of Zhao, and made Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，起復北府宰相，出知東京留守。

translations.literal: Upon his mother's death he entered mourning, but was recalled from mourning to become Chancellor of the Northern Commission and went out to serve as Military Governor of Dongjing.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he entered mourning, but was recalled from mourning to become Chancellor of the Northern Commission and was sent out as Military Governor of Dongjing.

sentences.zh: 會伐夏，孝友與樞密使蕭惠失利河南，帝欲誅之，太后救免。

translations.literal: When a campaign was launched against Xia, Xiaoyou and Commissioner Xiao Hui suffered defeat south of the Yellow River; the Emperor wished to execute them, but the Empress Dowager intervened and spared them.
translations.idiomatic: During a campaign against Xia, Xiaoyou and Commissioner Xiao Hui were defeated south of the Yellow River. The emperor wished to put them to death, but the Empress Dowager intervened and spared them.

sentences.zh: 復為東京留守，徙王燕，改上京留守，更王秦。

translations.literal: He again became Military Governor of Dongjing, was transferred to Prince of Yan, then changed to Military Governor of Shangjing, and his title was changed again to Prince of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: He again became Military Governor of Dongjing, was transferred to Prince of Yan, then made Military Governor of Shangjing, and his title was changed again to Prince of Qin.

sentences.zh: 清寧初，加尚父。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingning, he was given the honorific title Imperial Father.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Qingning he was given the honorific title Imperial Father.

sentences.zh: 頃之，復留守東京。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, he again served as Military Governor of Dongjing.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he again served as Military Governor of Dongjing.

sentences.zh: 明年，復為北府宰相。

translations.literal: The following year, he again became Chancellor of the Northern Commission.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he again became Chancellor of the Northern Commission.

sentences.zh: 帝親制誥詞以褒寵之。

translations.literal: The Emperor personally composed an edict to praise and honor him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally drafted an edict to praise and honor him.

sentences.zh: 以柴冊恩，遙授洛京留守，益賜純德功臣，致仕，進封豐國王。

translations.literal: Because of the merit of the imperial succession tablets, he was appointed in absentia Military Governor of Luojing, granted the additional merit title Pure Virtue, retired from office, and was advanced to Prince of Feng.
translations.idiomatic: In recognition of his service at the imperial succession ceremony, he received a remote appointment as Military Governor of Luojing, was granted the additional merit title Pure Virtue, retired from office, and was advanced to Prince of Feng.

sentences.zh: 坐子胡睹首與重元亂，伏誅，年七十三。

translations.literal: Because his son Hudu was the ringleader in Chongyuan's rebellion, he was executed; he was seventy-three years old.
translations.idiomatic: When his son Hudu led the rebellion of Chongyuan, he was executed on that account at the age of seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 胡睹在《逆臣傳》。

translations.literal: Hudu is treated in the 《Biographies of Rebellious Subjects》.
translations.idiomatic: Hudu is treated in the 《Biographies of Rebellious Subjects》.

sentences.zh: 蕭蒲奴，字留隱，奚王楚不寧之後。

translations.literal: Xiao Punu, style name Liuyin, was a descendant of Xi King Chubuning.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Punu, whose style name was Liuyin, was a descendant of the Xi King Chubuning.

sentences.zh: 幼孤貧，傭於醫家牧牛。

translations.literal: In youth he was orphaned and poor, hired out to a physician's household to herd cattle.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor in his youth, he was hired out to a physician's household to herd cattle.

sentences.zh: 傷人稼，數遭笞辱。

translations.literal: He damaged people's crops and was repeatedly flogged and humiliated.
translations.idiomatic: He trampled people's crops and was flogged again and again.

sentences.zh: 醫者嘗見蒲奴熟寐，有蛇繞身，異之。

translations.literal: The physician once saw Punu sleeping soundly with a serpent coiled around his body and regarded it as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Once the physician saw Punu sleeping soundly with a serpent coiled around his body and took it as an omen.

sentences.zh: 教以讀書，聰敏嗜學。

translations.literal: He taught him to read; Punu was clever and fond of learning.
translations.idiomatic: He taught him to read. Punu was quick-witted and eager to learn.

sentences.zh: 不數年，涉獵經史，習騎射。

translations.literal: Within a few years he had surveyed the classics and histories and practiced mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years he had read widely in the classics and histories and trained in horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 既冠，意氣豪邁。

translations.literal: After coming of age, his spirit was bold and lofty.
translations.idiomatic: After he came of age, his bearing was bold and spirited.

sentences.zh: 開泰間，選充護衛，稍進用。

translations.literal: During Kaitai, he was selected as a palace guard and gradually advanced.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaitai era he was selected for palace guard service and gradually won promotion.

sentences.zh: 俄坐罪黥流烏古部。

translations.literal: Soon he was convicted of a crime, tattooed as a criminal, and exiled to the Wugu tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was convicted of a crime, tattooed, and exiled to the Wugu tribe.

sentences.zh: 久之，召還，累任劇，遷奚六部大王，治有聲。

translations.literal: After a long time he was recalled, repeatedly assigned to demanding posts, promoted to Great King of the Six Xi Tribes, and gained renown for his governance.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was recalled, repeatedly given demanding assignments, and was promoted to Great King of the Six Xi Tribes, where his administration won wide praise.

sentences.zh: 太平九年，大延琳據東京叛，蒲奴為都監，將右翼軍，遇賊戰蒲水。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Taiping, when Da Yanlin seized Dongjing and rebelled, Punu was made Commissioner, commanded the right wing army, and met the rebels in battle at the Pu River.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Taiping, when Da Yanlin seized Dongjing and rebelled, Punu served as Commissioner, led the right wing, and met the rebels in battle at the Pu River.

sentences.zh: 中軍少卻，蒲奴與左翼軍夾攻之。

translations.literal: The center army fell back slightly; Punu and the left wing army attacked from both sides.
translations.idiomatic: When the center gave ground, Punu and the left wing struck from both flanks.

sentences.zh: 先據高麗、女直要沖，使不得求援，又敗賊於手山。

translations.literal: He first seized the strategic passes of Goryeo and the Jurchen, preventing them from seeking aid, and again defeated the rebels at Mount Shou.
translations.idiomatic: He first seized the strategic passes toward Goryeo and the Jurchen, cutting off their avenues of aid, and again defeated the rebels at Mount Shou.

sentences.zh: 延琳走入城。

translations.literal: Yanlin fled into the city.
translations.idiomatic: Yanlin fled into the city.

sentences.zh: 蒲奴不介馬而馳，追殺余賊。

translations.literal: Punu rode without saddle and chased down and killed the remaining rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Punu rode bareback in pursuit and cut down the fleeing rebels.

sentences.zh: 已而大軍圍東京，蒲奴討諸叛邑，平吼山賊，延琳堅守不敢出。

translations.literal: Soon the main army besieged Dongjing; Punu suppressed the rebel towns, pacified the bandits at Mount Hou, and Yanlin held firm and dared not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the main army besieged Dongjing. Punu suppressed the rebel towns and pacified the bandits at Mount Hou, while Yanlin held the city and dared not venture out.

sentences.zh: 既被擒，蒲奴以功加兼侍中。

translations.literal: After Yanlin was captured, Punu was given the additional title of Attendant Grand Master for his merit.
translations.idiomatic: After Yanlin was captured, Punu was given the additional title of Attendant Grand Master for his achievements.

sentences.zh: 重熙六年，改北阻卜副部署，再授奚六部大王。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Chongxi, he was made Deputy Deployment Commissioner of the Northern Zubu and again appointed Great King of the Six Xi Tribes.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Chongxi he was made Deputy Deployment Commissioner of the Northern Zubu and again appointed Great King of the Six Xi Tribes.

sentences.zh: 十五年，為西南面招討使，西征夏國。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he became Pacification Commissioner of the Southwest Circuit and campaigned west against the Xia state.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he became Pacification Commissioner of the Southwest Circuit and led a western campaign against Xia.

sentences.zh: 蒲奴以兵二千據河橋，聚巨艦數十艘，仍作大鉤，人莫測。

translations.literal: Punu took two thousand troops to hold the river bridge, gathered several dozen large warships, and also made great hooks; no one could fathom his plan.
translations.idiomatic: Punu took two thousand men to hold the river bridge, gathered several dozen large warships, and had great hooks fashioned as well, so that no one could guess his design.

sentences.zh: 戰之日，布舟於河，綿亙三十餘里。

translations.literal: On the day of battle, he arrayed boats on the river stretching continuously for more than thirty li.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of battle he spread boats across the river in a line more than thirty li long.

sentences.zh: 遣人伺上流，有浮物輒取之。

translations.literal: He sent men to watch upstream; whenever there was anything floating, they took it.
translations.idiomatic: He posted men to watch upstream and seize whatever floated down.

sentences.zh: 大軍既失利，蒲奴未知，適有大木順流而下，勢將壞浮梁，斷歸路，操舟者爭鉤致之，橋得不壞。

translations.literal: The main army had already been defeated, but Punu did not yet know. Just then a great log came floating downstream, about to destroy the pontoon bridge and cut off the route of retreat; the boatmen vied to hook it in, and the bridge was not destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The main army had already been defeated, but Punu did not yet know. Just then a great log came floating downstream, threatening to smash the pontoon bridge and sever the line of retreat. The boatmen vied to hook it in, and the bridge held.

sentences.zh: 明年，復西征，懸兵深入，大掠而還，復為奚六部大王。

translations.literal: The following year he again campaigned west, advanced deep with a detached force, plundered heavily and returned, and again became Great King of the Six Xi Tribes.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he campaigned west again, led a detached force deep into enemy territory, plundered heavily on the return march, and was again appointed Great King of the Six Xi Tribes.

sentences.zh: 致仕，卒。

translations.literal: He retired from office and then died.
translations.idiomatic: He retired from office and died.

sentences.zh: 耶律蒲古，字提隱，太祖弟蘇之四世孫。

translations.literal: Yelü Pugu, style name Tiyin, was a fourth-generation descendant of Su, younger brother of Emperor Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Pugu, whose style name was Tiyin, was a fourth-generation descendant of Su, the younger brother of Emperor Taizu.

sentences.zh: 以武勇稱。

translations.literal: He was known for martial courage and valor.
translations.idiomatic: He was famed for martial valor.

sentences.zh: 統和初，為涿州刺史，從伐高麗有功。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tonghe, he was Prefect of Zhuozhou and distinguished himself in the campaign against Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tonghe he served as Prefect of Zhuozhou and distinguished himself in the campaign against Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 開泰末，為上京內客省副使。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaitai, he was Deputy Commissioner of the Inner Guest Bureau at Shangjing.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Kaitai era he was Deputy Commissioner of the Inner Guest Bureau at Shangjing.

sentences.zh: 太平二年，城鴨淥江，蒲古守之，在鎮有治績。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping, when fortifications were built at the Yalu River, Pugu garrisoned them and achieved notable results in his command.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiping, when fortifications were raised along the Yalu River, Pugu held the post and won a strong record of governance.

sentences.zh: 五年，改廣德軍節度使，尋遷東京統軍使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was made Military Commissioner of the Guangde Army and soon transferred to Commander of Dongjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made Military Commissioner of the Guangde Army and soon transferred to Commander of Dongjing.

sentences.zh: 蒞政嚴肅，諸部懾服。

translations.literal: His administration was stern and grave; all tribes were awed into submission.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was stern and disciplined, and the tribes submitted in awe.

sentences.zh: 九年，大延琳叛，以書結保州。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, when Da Yanlin rebelled, he sent letters to win over Baozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, when Da Yanlin rebelled, he sent letters to win over Baozhou.

sentences.zh: 夏行美執其人送蒲古，蒲古入據保州，延琳氣沮。

translations.literal: Xia Xingmei seized the envoy and sent him to Pugu; Pugu entered and occupied Baozhou, and Yanlin's spirit was broken.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Xingmei seized the envoy and sent him to Pugu. Pugu then entered and took Baozhou, and Yanlin's morale collapsed.

sentences.zh: 以功拜惕隱。

translations.literal: For his merit he was appointed Tiyin.
translations.idiomatic: For this achievement he was appointed Tiyin.

sentences.zh: 十一年，為子鐵驪所弒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he was murdered by his son Tieli.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was murdered by his son Tieli.

sentences.zh: 夏行美，渤海人。

translations.literal: Xia Xingmei was a native of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Xingmei was a man of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 太平九年，大延琳叛，時行美總渤海軍於保州。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Taiping, when Da Yanlin rebelled, Xingmei was then commanding the Bohai army at Baozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Taiping, when Da Yanlin rebelled, Xingmei was then commanding the Bohai forces at Baozhou.

sentences.zh: 延琳使人說欲與俱叛，行美執送統軍耶律蒲古，又誘賊黨百人殺之。

translations.literal: Yanlin sent envoys to persuade him to rebel together; Xingmei seized them and sent them to the Commander Yelü Pugu, and also lured in a hundred rebel partisans and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Yanlin sent envoys to urge him to join the rebellion. Xingmei seized them and sent them to the commander Yelü Pugu, then lured in a hundred rebel partisans and put them to death.

sentences.zh: 延琳謀沮，乃嬰城自守，數月而破。

translations.literal: Yanlin's schemes were thwarted; he then sealed himself in the city to defend it, and after several months it was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Yanlin's plans were thwarted. He then shut himself in the city to hold out, and after several months it fell.

sentences.zh: 以功加同政事門下平章事，錫賚甚厚。

translations.literal: For his merit he was made Associate in the Department of Affairs with the title Equalizer-in-Chief, with very generous gifts.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was made Associate in the Department of Affairs with the title Equalizer-in-Chief and received lavish rewards.

sentences.zh: 明年，擢忠順軍節度使。

translations.literal: The following year he was promoted to Military Commissioner of the Zhongshun Army.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted to Military Commissioner of the Zhongshun Army.

sentences.zh: 重熙十七年，遷副部署，從點檢耶律義先討蒲奴裏，獲其酋陶得裏以歸。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Chongxi, he was transferred to Deputy Deployment Commissioner; following Inspector Yelü Yixian he campaigned against Punuli and captured its chieftain Taodeli and brought him back.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Chongxi he was made Deputy Deployment Commissioner. Following Inspector Yelü Yixian, he campaigned against Punuli, captured its chieftain Taodeli, and brought him back in triumph.

sentences.zh: 致仕，卒。

translations.literal: He retired from office and then died.
translations.idiomatic: He retired from office and died.

sentences.zh: 上思其功，遣使祭於家。

translations.literal: The Emperor remembered his merit and sent envoys to perform sacrifices at his home.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor remembered his service and sent envoys to offer sacrifices at his home.

sentences.zh: 論曰：不有君子，其能國乎？

translations.literal: The Commentary says: Without superior men, how could a state endure?
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Without superior men, how could a state endure?

sentences.zh: 方其擒延琳，定遼東，一時諸將之功偉矣。

translations.literal: When they captured Yanlin and pacified Liaodong, the achievements of the generals of that time were indeed grand.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanlin was captured and Liaodong pacified, the achievements of the generals of that hour were truly magnificent.

sentences.zh: 宜其撫劍抵掌，賈余勇以威天下也。

translations.literal: One would expect them to stroke their swords and strike their palms, selling their surplus courage to awe the world.
translations.idiomatic: One would expect them to stroke their swords and clap their palms, eager to spend their remaining valor in awe of the world.

sentences.zh: 蕭孝穆之諫南侵，其意防何其弘遠歟，是豈瞋目語難者所能知哉！

translations.literal: When Xiao Xiaomu remonstrated against the southern invasion, how far-reaching his intent and precautions were — how could those who glare and shout in debate understand this!
translations.idiomatic: Yet when Xiao Xiaomu remonstrated against the southern invasion, how far-reaching his foresight was — how could men who glare and shout in debate ever grasp it!

sentences.zh: 至論移風俗為治之本，親煩碎為失大臣體，又何其深切著明也。

translations.literal: As for his doctrine that transforming customs is the root of governance, and that attending to trivial details is beneath a great minister's dignity — how penetrating and lucid that was as well.
translations.idiomatic: As for his teaching that transforming customs is the root of governance, and that a great minister loses his proper stature when he busies himself with trifles — how penetrating and lucid that was.

sentences.zh: 為「國寶臣」，宜矣。

translations.literal: To call him a "national treasure minister" was fitting indeed.
translations.idiomatic: To call him a "national treasure minister" was only fitting.

sentences.zh: 孝先預弒仁德之謀，猶依城社以逃熏灌，為國臣蠹，雖功何議焉。

translations.literal: Xiaoxian took part beforehand in the plot to murder Empress Rende, yet still relied on the altars of state to escape punishment — a corruption upon the state's ministers; what merit of his could be discussed?
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoxian took part beforehand in the plot against Empress Rende, yet still sheltered behind the altars of state to escape punishment. He was a canker upon the realm's ministers; what merit of his could be weighed?
